review: Vehicle location procedures and every occupant-table cell transcribed. B555 occupant rows and component notes visually checked against the rendered page. Detailed damage rounding, wheel/arm integration and table extension remain pending.

entries.acceptance: Every vehicle has a body; other locations come from its actual component model. Deliberate location penalties combine with vehicle size, except deliberately targeting a draft creature uses that creature's size.

A random location that does not exist, is retracted or cannot be struck from that angle becomes body. If several valid alternatives match a random row, the attacker chooses among them; do not silently randomize that decision.
A powered vehicle taking a major body wound checks reliability; failure damages power or propulsion and halves movement.
Injury exceeding half maximum vehicle health cripples a track and sets ground movement to zero; discard excess injury using the detailed component cap.
A draft-animal result attacks the animal instead of the vehicle. Vehicle armor does not protect it and the vehicle takes no damage from this replacement hit.
An exposed-rider or open-cabin result attacks the actual occupant instead of the vehicle without vehicle armor. If unoccupied, resolve as body.
Injury above one-fifth maximum vehicle health cripples an exposed weapon/sensor mount; discard excess injury.
Injury above half maximum vehicle health cripples a wing; an airborne vehicle loses control and crashes, with excess component injury discarded.
Injury above one-third maximum vehicle health cripples a rotor; an airborne vehicle loses control and crashes, with excess component injury discarded.

A glass-location hit checks the occupant table. On an occupant hit, replace the vehicle hit with that occupant; a closed window supplies ceil(vehicle resistance/2). Distinguish this replacement from post-penetration debris injury.
A major wound to a large superstructure checks reliability; failure disables a specific authored important system within it.
A major wound to a main turret checks reliability; failure disables a specific major turret system or jams its rotation, as authored.

Injury above maximum health divided by twice total mast count cripples one mast, discarding excess. Lost sailing movement is one fraction per mast with the stated rounding; reconcile how rounding applies to current movement versus the loss before implementation.
Injury above one-third maximum health cripples a runner/skid, stops ground movement and topples a parked vehicle; excess injury is discarded.
Injury above one-third maximum health cripples a small superstructure or independent turret and disables contained equipment; excess is discarded.
A powered vehicle's vitals take double tight-beam burning or triple impaling/piercing wounding. Unpowered vehicles normally convert vitals to body; actual exceptional anatomy must be explicit.

Injury above maximum health divided by twice wheel count cripples a wheel; movement follows losing one leg from a creature with that many legs. Excess is discarded. Any tire injury also checks reliability; failure causes a disabling flat until changed.
Apply actual nonliving/homogeneous injury and combustible, flammable or explosive traits, rather than a universal vehicle injury multiplier.
Large-area injury affects the body and exposed occupants through the area-damage procedure; a random internal occupant check is not a substitute.

At least five penetrating damage to an occupied component prompts an occupant-hit check. On a hit, deal one die cutting per full five penetrating points, at a random personal location with personal armor. Vehicle damage remains separate.
If debris damage exceeds four dice, the author may distribute it among multiple occupants in packets of at most four dice; preserve total dice and selected recipients.

The occupant table uses the relevant vehicle/structure size and actual occupant count. Roll three dice at or below its number; this is not an ordinary skill check. Choose the struck person by a declared random or authored method.

The printed occupant grid spans size +1 through +11 and counts through five hundred, then says to continue. Resolve a tested extension rule and treatment of smaller sizes or empty compartments before supporting them; do not silently clamp.

Vehicle arms appear in random rows but have no separate injury paragraph on B554-B555. Resolve their threshold and effects through the detailed vehicle/object-anatomy rules before enabling arm damage.
